judgement.impact: Screen-reader user hears only "rating" and cannot learn the product is rated 4.3 out of 5 stars.
The blind user gets no rating value and cannot learn the 4-out-of-5 star score sighted users see.
Screen-reader user hears only "badge" and does not learn the product is on a 20% sale.
The blind user cannot tell that this thumbnail shows the black oval graphite product view and hears only the generic label photo 1.
Screen-reader user hears only Option 1 with no colour name or selected state, so cannot identify the black/Graphite option or choose the intended colour.
User cannot tell this swatch is the beige colour and cannot reliably choose the intended colour.
The user cannot tell that the second thumbnail shows a black square view and cannot confirm the product's appearance from that image.
User still understands the element is only a decorative outline and loses no product information or ability to act.
Screen-reader user cannot tell that Standard is currently selected and cannot verify the chosen size before adding to cart.
The user cannot tell that Option 3 is the blue colour option and cannot confidently select the intended colour, risking ordering the wrong variant.
Blind user does not know the sale price expires in about 2 hours and may delay purchase and lose the discount.
Blind user hears two prices without knowing R1,599 is the struck-out original price and R1,249 is the current price to pay.
The screen-reader user hears Close and cannot know the heart button saves to wishlist, so they will avoid it or expect it to dismiss the page.
The user cannot tell that the green dot means the product is in stock and available to order.
Screen-reader user hears only "More" and cannot identify, find, or voice-activate the visible Compare action.
